content.title: The Gospel Its Own Witness (1799)
content.author: Andrew Fuller
content.note: The English Baptist theologian's answer to the deism of Thomas Paine: the holiness and harmony of the gospel as evidence of its divine origin. For a Baptist reply to the Enlightenment's objections. Public domain: may be quoted, with the translator or edition named and an exact locator.
content.read: Held in this project's corpus: the Internet Archive text sources/library/bulk/ia/gospelitsownwitn00full.txt, and the 1799 first edition beside it. Not yet read for any article. 2026-11-27 (plan APOLOGETICS-FIELDS step 7): Part II, chapter I, pp. 125–132 (the prophecies of the Messiah) read in the held 1799 text for messianic-prophecy. Described, not quoted. 2026-11-27 (plan APOLOGETICS-FIELDS step 8, God & reality): the Introduction (pp. 1–3: reason as common ground; the internal evidence of Scripture and the Mithridate comparison) and Part I, chapter III (pp. 24–26: precepts aimed at the heart; love to God and neighbour) read in the held 1799 text for arguments-map and moral-argument; short sentences quoted, the long s modernised.
